newsitem.title: UK: Weaker Brent paper reflects sloppy wet market.
newsitem.headline: Weaker Brent paper reflects sloppy wet market.

text.p: Brent paper traded at easier levels in a quiet start to the week on Monday, tracking an oversupplied North Sea physical crude market, traders said.
Benchmark Dated Brent was heard offered at a 40 cent discount to July Brent, drawing offers at Dated -50 cents, but no physical trade was heard done as sellers wrestled with ample supplies.
"There is pressure on almost all grades," said one wet trader.
July/August Brent traded at -25 cents, and August/September for -20 cents, unchanged to slightly weaker than Friday.
Short-dated swaps or CFDS were showing a value of July Brent -55/-52 cents for the balance of this week, five cents adrift from Friday and softer than early Monday levels.

The following week's CFDs were talked at July -48/-41 cents, also five cents weaker. June 23-27 CFDs were talked at August Brent -61/-55 cents, equivalent to July -39/-33 cents or some nine cents below last week.
An Oseberg loading around June 18 was heard done weaker on Friday at a premium of two or three cents to Dated Brent. Forties was assessed at around Dated +15 cents, some five cents weaker.
In the Mediterranean, Urals was looking firmer on Monday after unconfirmed reports of a trade at Dated Brent -$1.25 a barrel cif Mediterranean on Friday.
The small cargo was very prompt and went to a refiner, traders said.
"The direction is certainly positive at the moment," said one. "There's nothing much available before June 20 and the margins are improving so demand is good," he said.
Urals cracking margins averaged $2.75 a barrel last week, nearly $1 better than the previous week, according to Reuters pricing data applied to industry standard product yields.
The absence of rival sour Iraqi Kirkuk Blend was also underpinning the spot market.

The U.N. oil-for-food deal was renewed last week for a second 180 day period but Iraq completed exports under the first round in late May and is unlikely to resume shipments until the third decade of June.
West European oil companies said they were still waiting for confirmation of contracts for the second tranche of exports.

In West Africans, Bonny Light was assessed unchanged at around Dated +42/+45 cents despite the presence of an estimated unsold 15 million June barrels. But Qua Iboe reflected a more widespread weakeness, assessed at around Dated +32/35 cents.
-- W Maclean, M Thompson London newsroom +44 171 542 7646
